title: Choose the A/B review layout
question: Which layout would make it easiest to judge the subtitle wording while both tracks stay visible over the same video?

options.label: Cinema-first review
options.thesis: Keep the video and both live subtitle overlays at the center of the review.
options.viewport: A compact experiment summary leads into a wide player; A appears over the image top, B at the bottom, with synchronized cue rows directly beneath.
options.risk: The cue list may need a tighter default height to keep the player in view.

options.label: Transcript-first compare
options.thesis: Make paired cue wording the main work area, with the shared video always in view.
options.viewport: A narrow sticky video sits beside a large timestamped A/B cue table; the selected cue is highlighted in both tracks.
options.risk: The video has less visual weight during playback.

options.label: Experiment bench
options.thesis: Compare the two tracks beside one shared player, with the test summary in the same view.
options.viewport: The video occupies the left half; the right half stacks A and B cue rows under a concise experiment summary and aligned-timing status.
options.risk: The simultaneous top-and-bottom overlays are smaller in the player.
